title: RegionPricingConfig
description: A (region, salesOrg) pair = one versioned, effective-dated config document. Adding a region or a sales org is adding one of these, never a code branch (requirements §5.1/§6). salesOrg "*" is a region-wide default that any sales-org-specific document overrides — see ConfigStore.getEffectiveAsOf.

salesOrg.description: A specific sales org id (e.g. "DE01"), or "*" for a region-wide default used when no sales-org-specific document applies.

supersedes.description: Version id this document replaces, if any.

resolution.description: Ladder: stockClass -> originOfData -> supplier/COO/OOD -> costBasis -> fallback chain. MROQ is routing input here, not a constraint.

costAccessSequence.description: TSS's own cost-source resolution order — not SAP's condition technique. An ordered list of source systems to try when a part has cost candidates from more than one, e.g. ["C4C", "ERP", "CCD", "CCP"] (C4C manual entry first, then ERP, then CCD, then CCP). The first system in the list with a candidate wins; matched against candidate.source.system by engine-core's resolveCandidate(). Optional — omitting it falls back to the facts' own `default` candidate id, same as before this existed.

stockClassMap.description: Maps this region's raw ERP stock-class codes (e.g. China's OMT/SMT/CMT, Americas' MTS-Z/MTS-2C) to the two canonical buckets buildUp/constraint `when` expressions branch on via item.stockClass. Optional — a region whose formulas don't yet vary by stock class (e.g. India, or Europe before Appendix A lands) omits it entirely, and srv skips classification for that region rather than requiring every part to carry a code. Once present, every priced item for that region must resolve to a mapped code or it comes back MISSING(STOCK_CLASS_UNRESOLVED) — silently skipping stock-class-conditioned elements would risk under-pricing.

fx.description: Explicit currency-conversion step: rate type, date, and position in the build-up sequence — never implicit in an adapter (requirements §5.3).
